name: Ophiuchus
introduction: is the Serpent-Bearer, often identified with Asclepius, the healer who could bring the dead back to life. He holds Serpens in his hands. Although it is not part of the traditional zodiac, the Sun passes through Ophiuchus in early December. It is best seen on northern summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Ophiuchus is full of remarkable neighbors. [Barnard’s Star](id:barnards-star), only 6 light-years away, has the fastest motion across the sky of any star. [Gaia BH1](id:gaia-bh1), about 1,560 light-years away, was the nearest known black hole when it was discovered in 2022.
In 1604, Johannes Kepler observed a supernova here, the last one in our galaxy seen with the naked eye.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Rasalhague](hip:86032), the head, is a white star 49 light-years away. [Sabik](hip:84012) and [Cebalrai](hip:86742) are nearby stars. [Zeta Ophiuchi](hip:81377) is a massive star racing through space, plowing a shock wave into the surrounding dust.
The double star [70 Ophiuchi](id:10pc-0115), 17 light-years away, consists of two orange dwarf stars that orbit each other every 88 years.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The [Rho Ophiuchi Nebula](id:ic-4604), one of the nearest star-forming regions, glows with colored dust. The dark [Pipe Nebula](id:cahlon-cloud-34) stretches nearby. Ophiuchus also contains seven globular clusters from Messier’s catalog, including M10 and M12.
